records.purpose: Copies one supported list/script record by zero-based kind ordinal in plugin/name order. Caller sets size >= sizeof(sco_content_item). Duplicate names retain distinct IDs. Failure leaves output untouched.
records.buffer_contract:
`sco_result (*item)(sco_plugin* self, sco_content_kind kind, uint32_t ordinal, sco_content_item* out);`
Copies one supported list/script record by zero-based kind ordinal in plugin/name order. Caller sets size >= sizeof(sco_content_item). Duplicate names retain distinct IDs. Failure leaves output untouched.
records.ownership: Caller-owned copied records/bytes; host owns bounded startup snapshot. No paths, borrowed content pointers or allocation transfer.
records.thread_affinity: Game thread only; synchronous memory copies, no callouts or file IO.
records.reentrancy: No callouts; callable from a game-thread consumer callback while runtime admission is open.
records.results: Query NOT_FOUND when absent; UNAVAILABLE when stopped/terminal shutdown; WRONG_THREAD off game thread; BAD_ARG invalid/released self or invalid buffer/kind; NOT_FOUND ordinal end or unknown/stale ID; read TOO_MANY reports needed bytes.
records.absent_capability: Query NOT_FOUND when service absent; no game capability required.
records.cleanup: No cancel or per-owner resource; host Stop clears snapshot and invalidates IDs. Table storage is process-lifetime; packs require restart.
limitations: List/script kinds only; script bytes are not permission to execute.

Hosts after SDK 2.4 RC1 also expose owned missions/<id>.scom declarations as Script (id: 1..100 lowercase ASCII letters, digits or underscores). RC1 does not discover them. Bytes remain opaque; private .cwmission/rules are not exposed and mission ingest availability is separate.
No C# or Lua binding. Windows file handling and gameplay unverified.

records.purpose: Copies exact immutable startup bytes; no added NUL. Size handshake: capacity in, written on OK, needed on TOO_MANY. NULL out requires zero capacity; empty file is OK/0. Only TOO_MANY changes size on failure; no failed call writes bytes.
records.buffer_contract:
`sco_result (*read)(sco_plugin* self, uint64_t id, void* out, uint32_t* inout_size);`
